nodes.description: An intro presentation of the project and its personal voice (BITB-077/082/083).
nodes.label: About / intro sheet

nodes.description: The /app landing page routes visitors to the Play Store or (on iOS) the add-to-home-screen PWA path.
nodes.label: App install landing page

nodes.description: Speak the question instead of typing it (BITB-120, Todo — not shipped anywhere).
nodes.label: Ask by voice (speech input)

nodes.description: The user is told the server is waking up instead of seeing a silent failure.
nodes.label: Backend cold-start / warm-up UX

nodes.description: Read a whole chapter behind a verse (GET /api/v1/scripture/chapter/{book}/{chapter}).
nodes.label: Chapter reading view

nodes.description: Ask a question and watch a streamed answer render; the request carries include_search + session_id; the metadata event arrives before content; the completion event carries citations, corrections, follow-ups and crisis resources.
nodes.label: Streaming chat over SSE (request fields + metadata/content/completion events)

nodes.description: After a few exchanges, an opt-in church finder searches nearby communities via POST /api/v1/church/search.
nodes.label: Church finder

nodes.description: Reach the team from the app via POST /api/v1/feedback/contact.
nodes.label: Contact form

nodes.description: Past conversations persist across launches and are readable with the network off (web: IndexedDB; Android: Room; both with export/import).
nodes.label: Conversation history, offline-readable

nodes.description: A structured card with locale- and country-appropriate hotline contacts on a crisis turn (BITB-255), driven by region + region_override request fields and the crisis_resources event.
nodes.label: Crisis resources card on self-harm turns

nodes.description: A user-triggered diagnostic report (collected logs) for support/debugging.
nodes.label: Diagnostic report export

nodes.description: Tapping a thumb starts a ~10s pending window with Undo and a quiet progress bar; one send per rating; thumbs-down shows a short notice that the message reaches the app's maintainer.
nodes.label: Feedback rethink window + maintainer-sharing notice (BITB-042)

nodes.description: Follow-up questions offered under an assistant answer (server-suggested via follow_ups, BITB-149/080), tappable to ask next.
nodes.label: Suggested follow-up question chips

nodes.description: Release notes readable in the app.
nodes.label: In-app changelog

nodes.description: A verse reference in the answer text is highlighted and tappable and opens the verse detail / chapter view (no need to scroll to the verse chips).
nodes.label: Tappable verse references inside the message body

nodes.description: BITB-085's recorded decision, restated as a BITB-087 AC: no Ko-fi/donate entry ships in iOS v1 (App Review risk + the maintainer's call); BITB-074 must not add one to the port.
nodes.label: iOS ships NO donate entry point

nodes.description: The iOS codebase must contain no chapter:verse regex — citations come from the citations-spans contract via text+occurrence substring search. Enforced by a CI grep, not reviewer diligence; a hand-written NSRegularExpression grammar is a rejected design (it would be the fourth dialect of audit finding A1).
nodes.label: iOS ships NO verse-reference regex

nodes.description: When the user typed in a language different from the selected UI language, a banner offers to switch (language_suggestion in the metadata event).
nodes.label: Language-mismatch switch banner

nodes.description: Bold, lists, blockquotes and inline code render as formatted text, not raw symbols.
nodes.label: Markdown rendering of assistant answers

nodes.description: Rate an assistant answer via POST /api/v1/feedback; optional inline comment.
nodes.label: Thumbs up/down feedback with optional comment

nodes.description: The app surfaces the no-network state and keeps readable content available (web: offline shell service worker; Android: NetworkMonitor + offline-readable Room history).
nodes.label: Offline / no-network handling

nodes.description: The web is an installable offline-shell PWA (BITB-102).
nodes.label: PWA installability (service worker + shell)

nodes.description: Platform on-device speech synthesis reads the streamed answer aloud, with localized verse speech normalization and a user "Show Listen button" preference.
nodes.label: Read the answer aloud (Listen button)

nodes.description: A floating control appears when the user scrolls up, jumping back to the latest.
nodes.label: Scroll-to-bottom affordance during streaming

nodes.description: A per-session message cap that ends with the same friendly take-a-break invitation across clients and offers a new session (BITB-023).
nodes.label: Session message limit with friendly "take a break"

nodes.description: A settings surface linking the legal pages and about content.
nodes.label: Settings with Privacy / Terms / About links

nodes.description: Share the answer text via the platform share sheet, or copy it to the clipboard.
nodes.label: Share an assistant answer (system share / copy)

nodes.description: A branded launch moment before the chat is interactive.
nodes.label: Splash / first-paint experience

nodes.description: User-controlled light/dark theme that persists.
nodes.label: Light/dark theme toggle

nodes.description: Choose the Bible translation answers quote from (KJV, WEB, ...).
nodes.label: Bible translation picker

nodes.description: Human-attestation tokens attach to POSTs (X-Turnstile-Token), are consumed single-use, and a 403 triggers exactly one reset + retry.
nodes.label: Turnstile token attachment + single-use + 403 retry-once

nodes.description: In-app language switching across en, it, de, es, fr, pt, ar, ru, zh, hi, ko.
nodes.label: UI language picker across 11 locales

nodes.description: Detecting verse references in streamed/user text exists in three parsers (backend, web, Android) that must stay in sync by boundary behavior, not just book lists (AGENTS.md).
nodes.label: Verse-reference detection in free text (the three parsers)

nodes.description: A consolidated verse panel over the conversation's scripture context, toggling between verses cited in the responses and all related verses.
nodes.label: Verses panel with Referenced / All-Related filter

nodes.description: A dismissible what's-new presentation on update.
nodes.label: "What's New" spotlight sheet

nodes.description: SSE streaming chat protocol: metadata event before content, content chunks, completion event (message_id, model, detected_translation, scripture_context, verses_cited, resolved_verses, corrected_message, corrections, follow_ups, language_suggestion, crisis_resources).
nodes.label: chat-stream-sse

nodes.description: Server-emitted citation spans (BITB-086): the completion event carries `citations` — where each verses_cited reference sits in the final answer text — so a client needs no verse regex of its own. Proven in the web client by BITB-109 (PR #1055).
nodes.label: citations-spans

nodes.description: Per-locale privacy/terms URLs. The web owns the pages; Android links into them with the user's UI locale (LegalUrls.kt); iOS v1 must do the same from Settings.
nodes.label: legal-urls

nodes.description: The clients request no OS permissions beyond the network: Android declares only INTERNET + ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE; iOS v1 must add no permission prompt (BITB-087 AC); web has no permission prompts (browser sandbox, mic-free).
nodes.label: permissions

nodes.description: Server-driven per-platform (web/android) feature flag registry on GET /config with explicit per-flag fail policies. Row reserved — status the cells when BITB-242 lands.
nodes.label: platform-flags

nodes.description: UI string catalog completeness across all 11 locales. Android completeness is enforced by the `translation-validation` CI job (.github/workflows/android-ci.yml); tools/parity-graph re-runs the identical check against the identical files (mechanically pinned — it reads the workflow's own extraction regex on every run), so the two can never silently disagree.
nodes.label: strings-catalog

nodes.description: Read-aloud telemetry funnel (BITB-247, PR #1226): clients POST {event, locale, platform, browser, os} with coarse fixed enums to /api/v1/client-events; never message text or IDs.
nodes.label: telemetry-os-enum

nodes.description: Shared verse-reference grammar (separators, range chars, fullwidth digits) generated from one fixture into web and Android, and reconciled by parity tests with the backend parser.
nodes.label: verse-grammar
